$comment: R0-23-WEB-R0-SCREENS: server responses the Release 0 screens are rendered against in jsdom.

journey.*: shaped from apps/server/test/release0-journey.integration.test.ts. Each body carries exactly the keys that suite asserts on that route, or on the same row elsewhere in the journey, and no other key. release0-journey.test.tsx holds the checked-in key list (JOURNEY_ASSERTED_SHAPES, with the line each key comes from) and asserts every body's key paths equal it, so a screen here can only read what the real-server journey proves.

The one exception is the tenant detail route GET /commerce/businesses/:b/invoices/:id (invoiceDraft, invoiceSent, invoicePartiallyPaid, invoicePaid): the journey never reads it (it reloads the row through the list route), and the server always adds paidAmount, remaining and the payment rows to that read (getInvoiceForBusiness, apps/server/src/modules/commerce/commerce.service.ts L669-683). Those bodies are the journey's row plus exactly the keys apps/server/test/commerce-invoice-detail.integration.test.ts asserts on that route (L225-227: payments, paidAmount, remaining on every read; L523-543: payments[].id, .amount, .status, and paidAmount = the SUCCESSFUL rows, remaining = total - paidAmount). The figures follow the journey: 0 paid on the DRAFT and SENT reads, the 100 cash payment (step 4), then the 150 settle (PAID).
screenOnly.*: responses a screen reads that the journey does not drive. Each names why it is outside the journey and where its shape comes from.
Ids carry the r023_ prefix; values mirror the journey (contact Ada Byron, CLIENT; INV-1001 with Consulting 2 x 100 and Setup 1 x 50 = 250 TTD; a 100 cash payment leaves 150).

login.why: The journey never signs in by password: it mints Supabase-shaped HS256 tokens and drives POST /identity/bootstrap. POST /identity/login proxies Supabase password sign-in (owner ruling D-02, hosted Supabase), so jsdom stubs it. Shape: the success return of IdentityController.login (apps/server/src/modules/identity/identity.controller.ts) and IdentityLoginResult (apps/web/src/lib/client.ts).

products.why: invoices/new loads the catalogue for its product picker; the journey invoices free-text items. Shape: the paginated envelope fetchProducts validates (apps/web/src/lib/client.ts).

timeline.why: invoices/[id] reads the activity timeline; the journey calls this route only as a denial probe (step 6) and asserts no owner body.

onboardingState.why: Onboarding is not a journey step (the journey bootstraps straight to a business). Shape: FRESH_STATE in apps/web/src/app/app/__tests__/onboarding-manual-path.test.tsx (R0-06).

forbidden.route: any business-prefixed route, as a non-member
forbidden.why: The journey asserts 403 on every business-prefixed route under another tenant (step 6) but not the body. Body: BusinessGuard's ForbiddenException('No access to this business') (apps/server/src/core/auth/business.guard.ts) through the global filter.

serverError.why: The journey's payments all land, so it never sees a failed submit. Step 4's retry case answers the first submit with this to prove a retry of the same form open reuses its idempotency key (R0-21). Body: the 500 branch of GlobalHttpExceptionFilter (apps/server/src/core/filters/http-exception.filter.ts), volatile envelope fields (timestamp, path, correlationId) left out.

gmailNotConfigured.why: The R0-07 contract: with no Gmail connection every Gmail send path answers this before any outbound call (apps/server/test/optional-services-fail-visibly.integration.test.ts, expectNotConfigured; GmailService gmailNotConfigured).

aiNotConfigured.why: The R0-07 contract for AI dispatch with no provider key (optional-services-fail-visibly.integration.test.ts: POST /ai/businesses/:b/ai/chat).
